subject: FORGE FINALE 48 -- rate floor derived (1,309), loop stopped, needs your call
body:
FORGE FINALE session 48 -- loop stopped on its own stall rule, with a question for you.

I derived the thing C3.2 has been blocked on since session 41: how many trades a reported win rate needs before it means anything. Every input came from your own constants, none from me -- break-even from SpecBreakevenWR's formula, the edge that has to be detectable from P6's own quarantine floor (expectancy 0.10R), and the confidence/power standard from the one the IC work already uses.

The answer is 1,309 trades. And every floor in the codebase is below it: 5, 8, 10, 15, 20, 30, and the largest at 500. Even at 500, the interval around a barely-tradeable win rate still overlaps break-even. So at every guard the system actually uses, a printed win rate cannot tell a real edge from a coin flip. That is exactly what the criterion was asking, and it now has an answer.

Enforcing it is easy -- all 118 rate lines now carry their own sample count, so one pass would do it. But in live operation those counts are in the tens to low hundreds, and the ghost validation caps at 299. Enforcing 1,309 would stop essentially every win rate in your log from printing. That guts the thing your logging rules exist to protect, and deciding it is your call, not mine at the end of an eleven-session day.

Three ways to go: (a) enforce it and accept the silence, (b) do what the Python side already does -- print the count and withhold the rate, so you still see the line and know why the number is missing, (c) rule that the criterion governs rates used as evidence rather than every log line, and amend it under the doc's own FF-45 path.

I'd take (b). It satisfies the criterion literally, you keep the line, and every withheld number tells you what it was withheld for.

Three sessions now with no criterion gained, which is the campaign's own stop rule, so I stopped rather than picking for you. Still 30/45. No build this session -- research layer only. Everything else left is either one of these decisions or waits for the market to reopen.
